headline: AI rout sends Treasury yields tumbling; yen and franc lead while the Aussie hits a one-year low
summary: The dollar index slipped about 0.1% to near 103.8, snapping an eight-day winning run, as a 5.3% Nasdaq plunge drove money into Treasuries and the 2-year yield fell 13bp to about 4.65%, eroding the dollar's rate edge. The yen and the franc led on haven buying and the rupee broke through 93 on record foreign inflows, while the Aussie, the won and the peso lagged as equity-linked currencies sold off.
drivers: Equity crash flips haven flows to the yen and franc

The Nasdaq fell 5.28%, the chip index 10.7% and the S&P 500 entered a correction, and Treasuries rallied: the 2-year fell 13bp to 4.65% and the 10-year slipped back below 5%. With the rate gap narrowing, USD/JPY dropped about 0.7% to near 158.5 and USD/CHF about 0.5% to near 0.8396, while AUD/USD lost about 0.6% to 0.6619.
Japan CPI adds to the yen's case

Core inflation rose to 2.2% in October, above the BoJ's 2% target for a second month, keeping a December hike in play just as US yields fell. Even Fed Governor Cook's call for tighter policy could not stop the dollar sliding against the yen.
Asia splits: tech exporters sell off, India draws inflows

The Kospi fell 5.2% and the Taiex 6.2%, pushing the won to 1,336.2 and the Taiwan dollar briefly through 33 before the central bank pulled it back to 32.936. The rupee jumped 62 paise to 92.67, a seven-month high, on record November foreign buying of Indian shares near $12bn.
view: Neutral overall, split by currency, for the next 1–2 weeks: the AI sell-off is pulling US yields lower, which helps the yen and franc, but it also hurts the Aussie and tech-linked Asian currencies, so I fade the dollar against the yen and back it against the Aussie and the loonie. I still hold the euro and sterling shorts with tight stops because the Fed is the only major bank still debating hikes. A 2-year yield below 4.50% would make me bearish the dollar broadly; a DXY close above 104.2 would revive the outright bullish view.
ideas: Hold the sale from 160.00–160.20, about 155 pips ahead, as US yields fall and Japan CPI firms; target 157.00, stop cut to 159.90.
Sell a bounce to 0.6660–0.6680 as the RBA is done and risk sours; for 0.6550, stop 0.6730.
Hold the long from 1.4080–1.4100, about 250 pips ahead, on the policy gap; for 1.4450, stop raised to 1.4290.
review: USD/INR hit its 92.80 target (close 92.67), about 85 paise banked, and USD/CHF was stopped at 0.8400 for roughly breakeven as the franc drew haven money. USD/JPY is about 155 pips in favour, EUR/USD about 205, USD/CAD about 250, GBP/USD about 85, the ringgit long about 0.025 and the rupiah long slightly ahead, so I hold and trail stops; the AUD re-sell at 0.6700 never filled, and EUR/JPY's close below 174 revives the short.

eurusd.note: Little changed near 1.0975 in a 1.0957–1.1000 range; the short is about 205 pips in favour.
eurusd.why: Two forces cancelled out. Lower US yields after the equity crash took some shine off the dollar, but the euro is a risk-sensitive currency too: the DAX fell 2.6% and the 2-year Treasury yield, even after a 13bp drop to 4.65%, still sits well above Bunds. The euro also hovered near its weakest since April 2025 as euro zone growth worries persist.
eurusd.outlook: I hold the short with the stop at 1.1020, above this week's 1.1010 high, for 1.0880: the Fed is still debating hikes while the ECB is on hold. A close above 1.1020 would say falling US yields have taken over.
eurusd.watch: Euro zone flash PMIs (Nov 25), ECB speakers, US PCE (late Nov), ECB (Dec 17).

view.call: Short from 1.1170–1.1190; Fed outpaces ECB, rally sold.

gbpusd.note: Flat near 1.3081 after fading a retail-sales pop to 1.3129; the short is about 85 pips in favour.
gbpusd.why: The pound moved on UK news, then gave it back. October retail sales rose 0.7% against a flat forecast, lifted by the government's stock-up campaign, and sterling briefly gained about 0.1%. It could not hold as the FTSE fell 1% and money went to the yen and franc rather than sterling, leaving it near a one-year low.
gbpusd.outlook: I stay short, cut the stop to 1.3150 above Friday's high, and keep 1.2950: the retail beat looks one-off and the BoE's next step is less certain than the Fed's. A close above 1.3150 would show sterling has turned.
gbpusd.watch: UK flash PMIs (Nov 25), UK budget headlines, BoE speakers, BoE (Dec 17).

view.call: Short 1.3150–1.3180; retail beat faded, BoE less hawkish.

audusd.note: Down about 0.6% to 0.6619, a one-year low (0.6609 at worst); my 0.6700 re-sell did not fill.
audusd.why: Risk did the moving. The Aussie is the market's favourite proxy for global growth, and a 5.3% Nasdaq plunge and a 10.7% drop in chip stocks hit it hardest among the majors. Thursday's 43,500 job loss had already convinced OCBC and others that the RBA is done at 4.85%, so there was no rate support to absorb the selling.
audusd.outlook: I lower the re-sell to 0.6660–0.6680, near Friday's high, for 0.6550 with a 0.6730 stop: the RBA is on hold and risk appetite is fragile. A close above 0.6730 would say the sell-off has run its course.
audusd.watch: Australia October CPI (Nov 25), RBA speakers, China data, global equities.

view.call: Sell 0.6660–0.6680; RBA done, risk appetite fragile.

usdjpy.note: Down about 0.7% to near 158.51 (low 158.41), below its 200-day average; my sale is about 155 pips ahead.
usdjpy.why: Both sides moved. The 2-year Treasury yield fell 13bp to 4.65% as investors fled stocks into bonds, cutting the dollar's rate edge, and Japan's core inflation rose to 2.2% in October, keeping a December BoJ hike on the table. Haven buying added to the yen's gain.
usdjpy.outlook: I hold the sale, extend the target to 157.00 and cut the stop to 159.90, just under 160: US yields are falling, Tokyo guards 160 and the BoJ is edging toward a hike. A close above 159.90 would mean dollar demand has returned.
usdjpy.watch: Tokyo CPI (late Nov), BoJ speakers, Japan's intervention data (Nov 30), US PCE (late Nov).

view.call: Sale filled 160.00–160.20; US yields fall, BoJ edging to hike.

usdchf.note: Down about 0.5% to near 0.8396 (low 0.8375); my long was stopped at 0.8400 for about breakeven.
usdchf.why: The franc did the moving. With US stocks crashing and Treasury yields down 11–13bp, the rate advantage that had kept the franc a funding currency shrank and haven buyers returned. The pair broke below 0.8400, the bottom of its recent range, before steadying into the close.
usdchf.outlook: I step aside in a 0.8340–0.8450 range: the Fed–SNB gap still favours the dollar, but haven demand will cap rallies while stocks are falling. A close below 0.8340 would open 0.8280.
usdchf.watch: Swiss CPI (early Dec), SNB comments, global equities, Fed (Dec 8–9).

usdcad.note: Little changed near 1.4341 after a 1.4299–1.4356 range; the long is about 250 pips in favour.
usdcad.why: Two forces cancelled out. Canada's retail sales beat, up 0.8% against 0.7% forecast with the core up 1.0%, and WTI rose 1.5% to about $83.70, which helped the loonie. But the equity crash hit risk-linked currencies, and the BoC's 2.50% rate against a Fed debating hikes keeps the rate gap wide.
usdcad.outlook: I hold the long for 1.4450 and raise the stop to 1.4290, below Friday's low: the policy gap is the widest of this cycle. A sharp oil rally, a tariff deal or a fall in US 2-year yields below 4.50% would be the main threats.
usdcad.watch: Canada Q3 GDP (late Nov), US–Canada tariff talks, oil, Fed (Dec 8–9).

view.call: Long from 1.4080–1.4100; rate gap widest of the cycle.

usdcnh.note: Offshore yuan recovered about 0.3% to near 6.674 after Thursday's slide toward 6.70.
usdcnh.why: The yuan did the moving, with help from Beijing. The PBOC set a steady fixing at 6.7131, signalling it wants to slow sharp moves after the post-summit volatility, and kept loan prime rates at 3.0% and 3.5%. Exporter dollar sales lifted the onshore yuan off a one-month low, and lower US yields helped.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep the 6.64–6.70 range: the PBOC is smoothing moves and exporters sell dollars on rallies. A close above 6.70 would open 6.75; below 6.64 would show the yuan regaining momentum.
usdcnh.watch: PBOC fixings vs estimates, US–China follow-up talks, China PMIs (Nov 30).

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC smoothing, exporters vs strong dollar.

usdhkd.note: Hong Kong dollar firmed to about 7.839, its strongest since Nov 9, as HIBOR rose across the curve.
usdhkd.why: Local rates did the moving. One-month HIBOR rose to 2.71%, a three-week high, and three-month HIBOR to 3.35%, its highest in a year, which made it less attractive to borrow Hong Kong dollars to buy US dollars. Lower US yields narrowed the gap further, and the pair moved off the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: tighter local liquidity pulls it off 7.85, but the gap to US rates still favours the carry trade. Only a sustained HIBOR squeeze would push it below 7.83.
usdhkd.watch: HIBOR, HKMA operations, month-end liquidity, Fed (Dec 8–9).

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; HIBOR up, carry still pays.

usdsgd.note: Little changed near 1.290, at the top of my 1.2780–1.2920 range.
usdsgd.why: Two forces cancelled out. Regional tech stocks crashed and Asian currencies weakened, but lower US yields and a firmer yuan took the edge off dollar demand. The MAS policy band, which steers the Singapore dollar against a trade-weighted basket, keeps it among the steadier Asian currencies.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2780–1.2920 range: the MAS band anchors the currency while risk-off flows support the dollar. A close above 1.2920 would open 1.3000.
usdsgd.watch: Singapore CPI and final Q3 GDP (late Nov), yuan fixings, Asian tech-stock flows.

usdkrw.note: Won fell 6.2 to 1,336.2 in Seoul after touching 1,340.3, as the Kospi plunged 5.2%; about 1,346 offshore.
usdkrw.why: Foreign stock selling did the moving. The Kospi lost 5.21% as AI worries hit Samsung and SK hynix, and foreigners sold a net 1.13 trillion won ($847m) of Korean shares, adding to dollar demand. Exporters sold dollars above 1,340, which limited the loss, but offshore trading pushed the pair toward 1,346 after the Nasdaq crash.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep the 1,330–1,365 range: exporter selling caps the pair, but chip-stock outflows look set to continue after the Nasdaq rout. A Seoul close above 1,365 would revive the long; below 1,325 would open 1,315.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows on Monday, Fed speakers, Korea November exports (Dec 1).

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar edged up 0.6 cents to 32.936 after another dip to 33.04, as the Taiex fell 6.2%.
usdtwd.why: The central bank did the moving again. The Taiex lost 2,394 points to a seven-month low, but foreigners sold only NT$9.4bn, far less than earlier in the week, and the central bank stepped in during the last half hour to pull the pair back under 33. Its FX chief said outflows are easing and that local residents sell more dollars once the rate passes 33.
usdtwd.outlook: I keep the 32.60–33.05 range: officials are clearly defending 33 with real money and outflows are slowing. A close above 33.05 would mean the defence has failed; below 32.60 would open 32.40.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows after the Nasdaq crash, central bank action near 33, central bank meeting (mid-Dec).

usdmyr.note: Ringgit flat at 4.1105/1150 at the 6pm KL close in a 4.1095–4.1180 range; my long is about 0.025 ahead.
usdmyr.why: Nothing decisive moved it. Bank Muamalat said traders stayed cautious before the Dec 8–9 Fed meeting, and technical indicators show the ringgit oversold, which limited further losses. Thursday's stronger Q3 GDP still supports it, but the Nasdaq crash came after the KL close and points to more pressure on Monday.
usdmyr.outlook: I hold the long for 4.150 with the stop at 4.090: Fed hike bets and the tech sell-off outweigh a steady Bank Negara. A close below 4.090 would say the break has failed.
usdmyr.watch: Malaysia October CPI (late Nov), oil and palm oil, regional chip stocks, Fed (Dec 8–9).

view.call: Long 4.080–4.090; Fed hike bets, tech sell-off.

usdphp.note: Peso lost 14.5 centavos to 63.81 at the BAP close as the PSEi hit its lowest since March 2020.
usdphp.why: Local stocks did the moving. The PSEi fell 3.1% to 5,306.98, its lowest close in more than six years, and RCBC's Ricafort also pointed to hawkish Fed signals. The peso traded 63.745–63.92, and a lower afternoon weighted average showed the pressure easing into the close.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 63.30–64.20 range with the record low as the cap: holiday remittances and cheaper oil help, but the stock slump and the Fed weigh. A close above 64.20 would mark a new record and open 64.80.
usdphp.watch: Oil, PSEi flows, BSP comments, BSP decision (Dec 17).

view.call: 63.30–64.20; remittances and oil vs stock outflows.

usdidr.note: Rupiah slipped 0.09% to 18,270, a record low; JISDOR 18,278. The long is slightly ahead.
usdidr.why: The dollar did the moving, slowly. Even after Bank Indonesia's surprise hike to 6.00% this week, the rupiah fell for a second day as the dollar held near a 19-month high and foreign investors kept selling ahead of MSCI index changes. It is now down about 8.9% this year.
usdidr.outlook: I hold the long for 18,500 and raise the stop to 18,180: the hike has not turned the tide and outflows persist. A close below 18,180 would show BI's defence is working.
usdidr.watch: BI intervention, MSCI changes (effective Nov 30), politics, Fed (Dec 8–9).

view.call: Long 18,200–18,250; record low despite BI hike, outflows.

usdinr.note: Rupee jumped 62 paise to 92.67, a seven-month high; my short hit its 92.80 target.
usdinr.why: Foreign inflows did the moving. Overseas funds have put about $12bn into Indian shares in November, the largest monthly inflow on record, as investors rotate away from AI-heavy markets, and lower oil prices and the RBI's special dollar window for oil firms cut dollar demand. Exporters rushed to sell dollars, and the RBI let the rupee rise.
usdinr.outlook: I book the short and switch to a 92.10–93.20 range: inflows remain strong, but the RBI may buy dollars to rebuild reserves after a $14bn weekly drop. A close below 92.10 would open 91.50; above 93.50 would signal a reversal.
usdinr.watch: Foreign equity flows, RBI dollar buying, oil, India Q3 GDP (late Nov), RBI decision (Dec 4).

view.call: 92.10–93.20; record inflows vs RBI dollar buying.

eurjpy.note: Down about 0.6% to near 173.96, below 174.0, as the yen gained; the short is back on.
eurjpy.why: The yen did the moving. Euro-dollar was flat, but USD/JPY fell about 0.7% as US yields dropped and haven buyers piled into the yen, and the DAX lost 2.6%. The cross closed below the 174.0 floor of my range, which I said would revive the short.
eurjpy.outlook: I re-sell at 174.0–174.5 for 172.0 with a 175.30 stop: the euro is weak and the yen has momentum from falling US yields and a possible BoJ hike. A close above 175.30 would end the call.
eurjpy.watch: Euro zone flash PMIs (Nov 25), Tokyo CPI (late Nov), Tokyo comments near 160.

cnhjpy.note: Down about 0.4% to near 23.75, low in my 23.6–24.2 range.
cnhjpy.why: The yen did the moving. The offshore yuan firmed about 0.3% on a steady PBOC fixing, but the yen gained more, about 0.7% against the dollar, on falling US yields and haven demand. Both currencies remain managed, so the cross mostly follows USD/JPY.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.6–24.2 range: the PBOC steadies the yuan while the yen's rally is capped by a still-wide rate gap. A close below 23.6 would mean the yen's strength is spreading.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, Tokyo CPI (late Nov), China PMIs (Nov 30).

view.call: 23.6–24.2; managed yuan, yen tracking US yields.

eurcnh.note: Down about 0.2% to near 7.324, mid-range in my 7.28–7.40 band.
eurcnh.why: The yuan did the moving. The euro was flat against the dollar, while the offshore yuan recovered about 0.3% on a steady PBOC fixing and exporter dollar sales, so the cross eased.
eurcnh.outlook: I keep the 7.28–7.40 range: euro weakness should resume, while the PBOC smooths yuan moves both ways. A close below 7.28 would open 7.24.
eurcnh.watch: PBOC fixings (daily), euro zone flash PMIs (Nov 25), ECB (Dec 17).

watch: Next: euro zone and UK flash PMIs and Australia CPI (Nov 25), the US Thanksgiving holiday (Nov 26), Tokyo CPI and US PCE (late Nov), Japan's intervention data (Nov 30), then the RBI (Dec 4), Fed (Dec 8–9) and ECB, BoE and BSP (Dec 17), plus Tokyo near 160 and Taiwan's defence of 33.
